topics.title: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910

outcomes.text: Listen to unfamiliar music from the Baroque concerto, Mozart opera and Romantic piano strands and describe its elements in musical language.
Analyse set work excerpts: effect of audience, time and place, how strands differ, composer purpose and links between elements and context.
Know the set concertos by Purcell, Vivaldi and Bach and their Baroque features.
Know the Act 1 numbers from Le Nozze di Figaro: overture, duettini, cavatina, arias and terzetto.

subtopics.title: Piano music of Chopin, Brahms and Grieg

outcomes.text: Know the set piano works by Chopin, Brahms and Grieg.
Describe melodic contour, intervals, ornaments, passing and auxiliary notes, and devices; identify diatonic and chromatic harmony, cadences, pedals and suspensions.
Identify modulations, enharmonic keys, binary, ternary, ritornello, sonata form, recitative and aria structures.
Describe orchestral and vocal timbres, string and piano techniques, textures from monophonic to fugal, tempo terms, syncopation, hemiola, and dynamics and articulation.
Read four to eight bar excerpts of unfamiliar music and about two pages of familiar scores; write melodic and rhythmic notation in all keys.
Identify standard and extended chords, inversions and secondary dominant sevenths, aurally and in notation, using correct terminology.
Choose two areas from pop, music for media, theatre, jazz, contemporary traditional and art music since 1910.
Listen to unfamiliar music by all named artists and appraise three artists per area using at least two published works and changes in style over time.
Read passages of up to eight bars, identify chords and symbols, and use terminology for the chosen areas.
Know the style of pop music and the named artists: Stevie Wonder, Joni Mitchell, Muse, Beyonce, Daft Punk, Labrinth.
Describe riffs, hooks, melisma, bends and slides, blue notes; power chords, sus4, extended chords and chord symbols.
Identify modes, pentatonic and blues scales; intro, verse, chorus, middle 8, bridge and breakdown.
Describe studio effects, instrument and vocal timbres, looping and layering, bpm, groove, backbeat and fades.

topics.title: Area of study 3: Music for media

outcomes.text: Know the style of music for media and the named artists: Bernard Herrmann, Hans Zimmer, Michael Giacchino, Thomas Newman, Nobuo Uematsu.
Describe leitmotif, extended and complex chords, tonal, atonal and modal writing.
Explain cue, underscore, mickey-mousing, diegetic and non-diegetic music; orchestral, electronic and ethnic timbres and effects.
Identify clusters, polarised texture, drones, additive rhythm, cross rhythm and rhythmic layering.

topics.title: Area of study 4: Music for theatre

outcomes.text: Know the style of music for theatre and the named artists: Kurt Weill, Richard Rodgers, Stephen Sondheim, Claude-Michel Schonberg, Jason Robert Brown.
Describe pitch bends, melisma, leitmotif, angular melody; power, sus4 and extended chords.
Identify song structures and orchestral, contemporary and vocal timbres and techniques.
Identify a cappella and colla voce textures, bpm and irregular metre.
Know the style of jazz and the named artists: Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, Pat Metheny, Gwilym Simcock.
Describe smears, falls, rips, glissandi; extended chords, tritone substitution and turn-arounds.
Identify blue notes, blues, pentatonic, octatonic scales, modal jazz, 12-bar blues, head, chorus and fours.
Describe mutes, growl, ghosted notes, big band instruments, heterophony, swing, push and drag, stop time.

topics.title: Area of study 6: Contemporary traditional music

outcomes.text: Know the style of contemporary traditional music and the named artists: Astor Piazzolla, Toumani Diabate, Anoushka Shankar, Mariza, Bellowhead.
Describe raga, kumbengo, birimintingo, drones, sus4 chords and modes.
Identify tango nuevo, milonga, fado, alap, fusion, folk rock; bandoneon, kora, sitar, Portuguese guitar and tango string techniques.
Identify looping, layering, heterophony, polyrhythm, 3+3+2, habanera and tala.

topics.title: Area of study 7: Art music since 1910

outcomes.text: Know the style of art music since 1910 and the named artists: Dmitri Shostakovich, Olivier Messiaen, Steve Reich, James MacMillan.

subtopics.title: Art music melody, harmony and tonality

outcomes.text: Describe modes of limited transposition, tone rows, resultant melody, metamorphosis, non-functional and static harmony, clusters, bitonality and atonality.
Identify cyclical structures, ostinato, cadenza; organ stops, ondes Martenot, studio effects and extended techniques.
Identify looping, layering, drones, additive and palindromic rhythms, metrical displacement, phasing, augmentation and diminution.
Perform at least ten minutes as an instrumentalist or vocalist, solo or in ensemble, and/or through music production.
Choose repertoire by the demand of your own part and play pieces with composer-intended accompaniment accompanied.
Show control of pitch, rhythm, tone and ensemble, and tempo, dynamics, phrasing and articulation, with understanding of style and the composer's purpose.
Realise a pre-existing piece with MIDI and audio tracks, at least five student-input tracks, with good capture and dynamic processing.
Supply a score, lead sheet, guide recording or annotation with each performance recording.
Develop and manipulate musical ideas into two musically convincing compositions: one to an externally set brief, one free.
Compose at least four and a half minutes in total, as notated or lead sheet work, or digital production with annotation.
Use musical elements with technical control and creativity in your chosen style or genre.
Write a 150-word programme note for each piece on intention and audience, list software and hardware, and supply score, lead sheet or aural guide.
